title: Unbounded coefficient comparison on flat-term K-flat inverse-image models
statement:
Let $f:V\to X$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $A\to B$ a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and canonical inverse images $f_A^*,f_B^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], which are exact [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] and induce $D(f_A^*),D(f_B^*)$ termwise. Let $K$ be an arbitrary, possibly unbounded, object of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived coefficient extension $-\otimes_A^L B$ takes values in the derived category of $B$-modules [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], $f_A^*P$ is flat-term K-flat and represents $D(f_A^*)K$.

The complexes $(f_A^*P)\otimes_{A_V}B_V$ and $f_B^*(P\otimes_{A_X}B_X)$ represent, respectively, $(D(f_A^*)K)\otimes_A^L B$ and $D(f_B^*)(K\otimes_A^L B)$. There is a natural $B_V$-linear chain isomorphism
$$t_P:(f_A^*P)\otimes_{A_V}B_V\xrightarrow{\sim}f_B^*(P\otimes_{A_X}B_X).$$
Under the canonical constant-ring identifications $f^{-1}A_X\cong A_V$, $f^{-1}B_X\cong B_V$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], both sides identify with $f^{-1}P\otimes_{f^{-1}A_X}B_V$, and $t_P$ is the identity on local pure tensors $p\otimes b$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Its localization is independent of the flat-term K-flat resolution and gives the canonical derived inverse-image coefficient comparison, a natural isomorphism
$$(D(f_A^*)K)\otimes_A^L B\xrightarrow{\sim}D(f_B^*)(K\otimes_A^L B)$$
in $D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$. No flatness of $A\to B$, boundedness, constructibility or finite Tor amplitude of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: For any supplied flat-term K-flat P, apply the ringed-topos pullback theorem with the algebraic inverse image and canonical constant-ring comparison. This gives both K-flatness and termwise flatness of the pulled complex. Exact inverse image preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The universal coefficient counits on P and its pullback are invertible, so the two computation morphisms are isomorphisms.
